# A window under an `if` that reads state comes and goes with it only where the
# platform can create and destroy a window while the program runs
# (`#[gen.can(windowLifetimes)]`: gtk4 and fyne). Everywhere else it is refused
# at the window, rather than emitted as if the `if` were not there -- which is
# what every target did before, gtk4 included.

! sngl generate --lang none --platform html -o html app.sngl
stderr 'app.sngl:10:14: a window under an `if` that reads state is created and destroyed with it, which html cannot do'

! sngl generate --lang go --platform bubbletea -o tea app.sngl
stderr 'app.sngl:10:14: a window under an `if` that reads state is created and destroyed with it, which bubbletea cannot do'

# A condition that reads no state is not a lifetime, and builds anywhere.
sngl generate --lang none --platform html -o html2 const.sngl

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

var details = false

ui.window #main(title="Main") {
    ui.button(text="Details", @click { details = !details })
}

if details {
    ui.window(title="Load") {
        ui.text(value="load")
    }
}
-- const.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

const wide = true

ui.window #main(title="Main") {
    ui.text(value="main")
}

if wide {
    ui.window(title="Wide", href="/wide.html") {
        ui.text(value="wide")
    }
}
